text:
Liam: hey team, first-day snag. Trying to do onboarding from a cafe but their captive portal blocks outbound TCP until I accept terms. VPN connects, ssh to bastion starts but then stalls because the portal intercepts. browser auth works, but CLI traffic (ssh, docker pull) times out until the portal is accepted. Anyone have a clean flow for captive portals + split-tunnel?

Priya: welcome Liam! Captive portals are annoying with VPNs because the client sends VPN traffic but the packet path is NATed/intercepted before the TLS handshake completes. Quick trick: open the portal in your phone, accept, then reconnect VPN. If you can9t open the portal from the machine, try `curl http://neverssl.com` in the terminal to trigger the redirect and accept it in the browser.

Liam: I can open the portal in browser on the same laptop and accept, but after that the VPN still fails to route internal hosts until I kill/restart the vpn client. Is there a way to refresh routes without full reconnect?

Omar: depends on the client. For WireGuard-based clients you often need to bring the interface down/up to re-apply allowed-ips. On mac: `sudo ifconfig utun0 down; sudo ifconfig utun0 up` (or use the client GUI toggle). For OpenVPN you can `sudo systemctl restart openvpn-client@redwood` or send a `SIGHUP` to reload. But restarting is common.

Liam: restarting works but it's clumsy during a meeting. Any approach that avoids full restart?

Priya: you can script route refresh: when you detect captive portal from DNS/curl failure, run a small script that flushes default routes and re-adds VPN routes. Example snippet we use in onboarding: `sudo route -n flush; sudo route add -net 10.10.0.0/16 -interface utun0` (varies by platform). We should add distro-specific snippets to onboarding.

Jen: if the cafe requires browser auth on a different device (e.g., phone hotspot login), you can tether after auth or use phone to accept then iCloud/Google sync to browser - hacky but works. For docker specifically, note Docker Desktop may cache failed DNS results; restarting Docker after establishing connectivity sometimes needed.

Liam: good call, docker stalled even after ssh came back. Restarting Docker Desktop fixed it.

Omar: another long-term trick: use our dev-proxy (HTTPS) which tunnels registry and web traffic over TLS 443 and is usually allowed through captive portals. We also have the web-bastion (browser SSH) which works over port 443 and survives captive portal flows more often.

Liam: web-bastion would be perfect. I tried it but got 403 on the first day. Is that an access delay?

Infra-bot: Automated note: new-hires get web-bastion permission after identity sync (~1 hour). If blocked longer, please open a ticket. See https://redwood.internal/onboard/access (bot).

Liam: ok, will wait. Two asks: 1) can infra add a small captive-portal troubleshooting section in onboarding (curl trick, route refresh commands)? 2) is there a recommended script for route refresh per-platform?

Priya: yes to both. I'll add a compact mac/linux/windows script to onboarding. For Windows PowerShell you can `Get-NetRoute` and `Remove-NetRoute`/`New-NetRoute` to refresh. For Mac/Linux we9ll add `ifconfig`/`ip route` examples.

Omar: also filing a ticket to consider exposing dev-proxy on 443 and documenting that it is the fallback for captive environments.

Infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-5412 "Onboarding: captive portal troubleshooting and dev-proxy as fallback" (https://redwood.internal/infra/5412)

Liam: thanks everyone, adding notes to my onboarding checklist. Will use web-bastion/dev-proxy next time. :thumbsup:
